continuity.campaign_development: May 59 BCE: Surrounding landholders unanimously grant Gaius Maximus Valerius ownership of the former bandit-held lands seized during the expedition. They state that they lack the labor, resources, and time to restore the damaged properties into workable estates and credit Valerius with restoring their livelihoods. Ownership is established in principle, but the exact acreage of the transferred lands has not yet been surveyed and therefore does not alter the measured land-area metric. Valerius begins organizing restoration while maintaining the Roman force at 398 men.
continuity.land_area_history: Round 33 establishes 4.00 square miles of measured pre-existing holdings; Round 42 adds 0.25 sq mi of confirmed acquisitions. Round 53 establishes ownership of all former bandit-held lands seized during the campaign, but their aggregate area remains unmeasured pending survey, so measured land_area_sq_miles remains 4.25 sq mi.

event_variety_policy.rule: Do not make every event about the same subject. Prefer distinct news dimensions supported by current state: military operations, intelligence, logistics, political relationships, economic/property activity, social/local developments, personal developments, geography, and reactions.
